A practical approach is to set tolerances by item risk and value: allow a small recount tolerance for low-risk items, but use tighter limits for high-value or controlled stock. Recount before escalating; escalate confirmed variances above a set quantity or value, and also repeated smaller variances or unexplained patterns. Pilot the thresholds, then adjust them using actual count and recount results.

Set the thresholds by item value and recount history, not one flat rule. First, measure normal counting noise from recent recounts and set a tolerance a little above it, for example a few units or a small percentage for low-value stock. Variances inside that tolerance get logged but not investigated. Tighter limits suit high-value or fast-moving items. Any variance above tolerance triggers a blind recount by someone else. Escalate only if the variance survives the recount, exceeds a higher value limit, or recurs over several cycles. Review the thresholds each quarter so they track real patterns.
